# Worked example (test fixture, not a result)

The hand-computed case from [RFC-0004 §Worked example](../../../../../rfcs/0004-metrics-timing-grades.md#worked-example-test-fixture-not-a-result). The inputs are invented round numbers and describe no system. `inputs.json` holds the events, release times and recorded metrics; `expected.json` holds the values computed by hand in the RFC table. `run.json` is the same case as a run record whose derived values `iproofs derive --check` recomputes from their stored inputs, with `reference.yaml` (price 3.6 USD/gpu_hour, 1 GPU) and `workload.yaml` (8e9 active parameters) as fixture inputs. Tests compare with `math.isclose(rel_tol=1e-12)` because a decimal such as 0.01 has no exact binary64 form.
